mainTopic: Benefiting from burning impure תרומה; forbidden lamp fuels (tar, צרי) on שבת; נר שבת as a חובה and washing as a מצוה; aggadot on lost comforts in exile and on who is wealthy
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier question: why may one benefit from burning impure תרומה but not from burning impure קדשים? The גמרא answers that קדשים has more strict rules, or that eating it while impure carries כרת. רב נחמן בר יצחק adds a פסוק, "תתן לו", which implies that impure תרומה is fit for the כהן's fire. Next the גמרא explains רבי ישמעאל's ban on lighting with tar. רבא says the bad smell might make a person leave the light, and that matters because נר שבת is a חובה. רב rules that washing in hot water before שבת is optional, and another אמורא calls it a מצוה. He proves this from the custom of רבי יהודה בר אלעאי, which leads to a side story about his students and ציצית on linen. The גמרא then brings a פסוק from איכה about the comforts an exile loses, such as the נר שבת, bathing and a good bed. A ברייתא follows with four views on who is truly wealthy. The amud ends with רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's ban on lighting with balsam sap (צרי), רבה's reason for it, and the start of אביי's reply, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: More strict rules of תרומה: no redemption, forbidden to non-כהנים
steps.stepSummary: The end of the challenge. תרומה cannot be redeemed and is forbidden to non-כהנים, so why treat קדשים as stricter?
steps.simpleTranslation: And תרומה cannot be redeemed, and it is forbidden to non-כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a list it started on the previous amud. The list names ways that תרומה is actually stricter than קדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier question was why burning impure קדשים may not be used for benefit while burning impure תרומה may. These two points add to the challenge. קדשים can sometimes be redeemed and eaten by non-כהנים, but תרומה never can.

keyTerms.meaning: Redemption, meaning making something holy into regular (חולין) by paying for it
Non-כהנים, people who are not priests
The portion of produce given to a כהן

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question. It is the end of a challenge that began on the previous amud. The גמרא is still listing ways that תרומה is stricter than קדשים.

phrases.english: and it is forbidden to non-priests.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a challenge that started on the previous amud
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that קדשים is stricter than תרומה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: תרומה has strict rules that קדשים lacks, so we cannot simply assume קדשים is stricter.

steps.title: קדשים has more strict rules
steps.stepSummary: Answer: the strict rules of קדשים are more numerous.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those [the strict rules of קדשים] are more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by counting. קדשים has more strict rules than תרומה, so it is fair to treat it as the stricter one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not deny that תרומה has its own strict rules. It weighs the two lists against each other, and the list for קדשים is longer. So the strictness about benefit goes to קדשים.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Weighing: count the strict rules on each side
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since תרומה has strict rules too, maybe it is equally strict
steps.terutzMaskana: קדשים has more strict rules, so it counts as stricter

steps.title: Another answer: קדשים carries כרת
steps.stepSummary: A second answer. Eating קדשים while impure is punished with כרת, which is harsher than the punishment for תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: קדשים is stricter because one is punished with כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer that does not depend on counting rules. One rule settles it: the punishment for קדשים is harsher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating קדשים while impure is punished with כרת. Eating תרומה while impure is punished with מיתה בידי שמים, which is a lighter punishment. That single difference in punishment shows that קדשים is more severe.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say (introduces another answer)
Spiritual cutting off, a severe punishment from Heaven

phrases.english: Consecrated items are stricter, since [eating them impure] is punishable by karet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the same challenge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: תרומה might be equal to קדשים in strictness
steps.terutzMaskana: The כרת punishment makes קדשים clearly stricter

steps.title: A פסוק shows impure תרומה is for the כהן's fire
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק learns from "תתן לו" that impure תרומה may be used for the כהן's fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: The פסוק says "you shall give him." To him, meaning for eating, and not for his fire. This implies that impure תרומה is fit for his fire.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives a different source, a פסוק, for the rule that one may benefit from burning impure תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק "תתן לו" teaches that a person must give the כהן pure תרומה that he can eat. He should not give תרומה that is only good for burning. Since the פסוק points to תרומה that is "for his fire," it shows that impure תרומה is meant to be burned for the כהן's benefit.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the rule a source in the תורה itself, instead of only a comparison of how strict קדשים and תרומה are.

phrases.english: the verse says: "You shall give him."
By implication, it [impure teruma] is fit for his fire.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר, אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different approach based on a פסוק
steps.raayaObject: That one may benefit from burning impure תרומה
steps.whatToRemember: One may benefit from burning impure תרומה. Reasons given: קדשים is stricter (more rules, or כרת), or the פסוק "תתן לו... ולא לאורו" implies impure תרומה is for the כהן's fire.

steps.title: Why does רבי ישמעאל forbid lighting with tar?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the reason for רבי ישמעאל's ruling in the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל says, etc. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic in the משנה. רבי ישמעאל forbids lighting the שבת lamp with tar, and the גמרא asks why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tar burns well, so the problem is not that it fails to give light. The גמרא wants to know what is wrong with it.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc., the rest of the משנה
Tar, the fuel רבי ישמעאל forbids

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic from the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason tar is forbidden for the שבת lamp

steps.title: רבא: bad smell, so one may leave the light
steps.stepSummary: Tar smells bad, so the חכמים made a rule. Otherwise a person might leave the light and walk away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Since its smell is bad, it is a decree, lest he leave it and go out.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains that tar has a bad smell. The person might not want to sit near it and could leave the room.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban is a גזירה, a protective rule made by the חכמים. It is not a direct prohibition from the תורה. The worry is that the person will not stay near the light.

keyTerms.meaning: A protective rule made by the חכמים

phrases.english: it is a decree, lest he leave it and go out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 5
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה, because the bad smell may make him abandon the light

steps.title: אביי: so let him leave
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges: what is wrong with leaving the light?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: So let him leave!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבא's reason. Why should we care if the person walks away from the lamp?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's reason only works if there is a requirement to stay near the light. אביי is pointing out that no such requirement has been shown.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him: So let him leave!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's answer
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is no obligation to sit by the light, so leaving it is not a problem.

steps.title: רבא: נר שבת is an obligation
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that lighting the נר שבת is a חובה, so one must stay and benefit from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Because I hold that lighting a lamp on שבת is an obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains why leaving the lamp matters. Lighting the שבת lamp is required, so it must actually be used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since נר שבת is a חובה, the person should eat by its light in honor of שבת. If he walks away, he loses this obligation. That is why the חכמים did not allow a fuel that smells bad.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֲנִי אוֹמֵר הַדְלָקַת נֵר בְּשַׁבָּת חוֹבָה.
phrases.english: Because I say that kindling a lamp on Shabbat is an obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁאֲנִי אוֹמֵר הַדְלָקַת נֵר בְּשַׁבָּת חוֹבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reveals a hidden assumption: lighting is a חובה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Lighting is optional, so leaving the light does not matter
steps.terutzMaskana: Lighting is a חובה, so one must stay by the light

steps.title: רב: lighting is a חובה, washing is optional
steps.stepSummary: Support from רב: lighting the נר שבת is a חובה, while washing in hot water before שבת is רשות.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב נחמן בר רב זבדא said (and some say רב נחמן בר רבא said) in the name of רב: Lighting a lamp on שבת is an obligation. Washing hands and feet in hot water before evening is optional.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רבא with a statement of רב saying that lighting the נר שבת is a חובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב compares two things people do to prepare for שבת. Lighting is required. Washing with hot water is only רשות, meaning optional. There are two versions of who passed on this statement from רב.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (a second version of who said it)

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר רַב זַבְדָּא,
phrases.english: As Rav Naḥman bar Rav Zavda said,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר רָבָא
phrases.english: and some say Rav Naḥman bar Rava said,
Kindling a lamp on Shabbat is an obligation;
washing hands and feet with hot water in the evening

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר רַב זַבְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's claim in step 8
steps.raayaObject: That נר שבת is a חובה

steps.title: But washing is a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The אמורא who passed on רב's statement adds his own view: washing before שבת is a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I say: it is a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The אמורא who reported רב's words now adds his own opinion. Washing in hot water before שבת is more than optional. It is a מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets up a middle level between required and optional. A מצוה is good and praiseworthy to do, even though one is not obligated to do it.

keyTerms.meaning: A praiseworthy act, more than optional but less than an obligation
And I say (the speaker's own view)

steps.confusionAlert: Here מצוה does not mean an obligation. It sits between רשות (optional) and חובה (required).

phrases.english: And I say: it is a מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds to רב's ruling about washing
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Washing in hot water before שבת is a מצוה

steps.title: What kind of מצוה is washing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what makes washing a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the מצוה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the basis of calling washing a מצוה. This sets up the story that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If washing is not required, the גמרא wants to know what source shows it has the status of a מצוה.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the claim in step 10
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What makes washing before שבת a מצוה

steps.title: The custom of רבי יהודה בר אלעאי
steps.stepSummary: Every ערב שבת, רבי יהודה בר אלעאי washed with hot water and wrapped himself in garments with ציצית. He looked like an angel.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יהודה said in the name of רב: This was the custom of רבי יהודה בר אלעאי. On ערב שבת they would bring him a tub full of hot water. He would wash his face, hands, and feet, wrap himself, and sit in linen garments with ציצית, and he looked like an angel of ה' צבאות.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer is the practice of a great תנא. He washed in hot water every ערב שבת to honor שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A great צדיק made a regular habit of washing to honor שבת. This shows the washing is a מצוה and not just a matter of choice. It does not make it a required חובה.

phrases.english: As Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ הָיָה מִנְהָגוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בַּר אִלְעַאי,
phrases.english: This was the custom of Rabbi Yehuda bar Elai:
on Shabbat eve they would bring him
a tub full of hot water,
and he would wash his face, hands, and feet,
and wrap himself, and sit in linen cloaks with fringes,
and he resembled an angel of the Lord of hosts.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: כָּךְ הָיָה מִנְהָגוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The regular practice of רבי יהודה בר אלעאי shows that washing is a מצוה
steps.whatToRemember: נר שבת is a חובה. Washing in hot water before שבת is a מצוה, as shown by the practice of רבי יהודה בר אלעאי.

steps.title: The students hide their corners and are rebuked
steps.stepSummary: The students hid the corners of their garments, which had no ציצית. רבי יהודה reminded them that the הלכה follows בית הלל, who require ציצית on linen.
steps.simpleTranslation: His students would hide the corners of their garments from him. He said to them: My sons, did I not teach you that for a linen garment with ציצית, בית שמאי exempt it and בית הלל obligate it, and the הלכה follows בית הלל?
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues with a side point. רבי יהודה challenges his students for not putting ציצית on their linen garments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wool ציצית on a linen garment makes כלאים (שעטנז). בית שמאי therefore exempt linen garments from ציצית. בית הלל say the מצוה of ציצית overrides כלאים and require it, and the הלכה follows them.

keyTerms.meaning: A linen garment with regard to ציצית

phrases.english: And his students would hide from him
He said to them: My sons,
did I not teach you this:
a linen cloak with regard to fringes:
and the halakha follows the words of Beit Hillel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן: בָּנַי, לֹא כָּךְ שָׁנִיתִי לָכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story with a side point about ציצית
steps.kashyaTarget: The students' practice of not putting ציצית on linen
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The הלכה follows בית הלל, who require ציצית on linen garments.

steps.title: The students' reason: a decree because of night garments
steps.stepSummary: The students held that the חכמים forbade ציצית on linen because of garments worn at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they held: it is a decree because of a night garment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the students did not follow בית הלל. They held that the חכמים made a protective rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no מצוה of ציצית at night. So a linen garment with wool ציצית worn at night would be plain כלאים with no מצוה to override it. To avoid this, the חכמים forbade wool ציצית on linen altogether, even though the תורה allows it.

keyTerms.meaning: A forbidden mixture of wool and linen

steps.confusionAlert: The students did not disagree that the הלכה follows בית הלל on the תורה level. They held there is an extra rule of the חכמים forbidding it.

phrases.english: it is a decree because of a night garment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the students' side against the challenge in step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: A rabbinic decree on top of the תורה law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The students were simply ignoring בית הלל
steps.terutzMaskana: They held that the חכמים forbade it because of garments worn at night

steps.title: A verse about exile is quoted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a פסוק from איכה: 'My soul is removed far from peace; I forgot goodness.'
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And my soul is removed far off from peace, I forgot goodness.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a verse so that it can explain it in the next steps. This is a setup line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא has just been talking about the pleasure of washing in hot water before שבת. This verse describes the comforts an exiled person has lost. The verse has two halves, and each half will be explained separately.

keyTerms.meaning: And it was cast away / removed far off

phrases.english: "And my soul is removed far off from peace,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connects to the theme of washing in hot water before שבת and brings in a related verse
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The verse is presented as the base text for the explanations that follow.

steps.title: What is the lost 'peace'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'my soul is removed far from peace' refers to.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'And my soul is removed far off from peace'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the first half of the verse means. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Peace' in the verse is vague. The גמרא wants to know which specific thing the exile lost that is called 'peace.'

phrases.english: What is "And my soul is removed far off from peace"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the first half of the verse just quoted

steps.title: The lost peace is lighting the שבת lamp
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו says the lost 'peace' is lighting the נר on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: This is lighting a lamp on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers that the 'peace' the exile lost is the chance to light שבת candles.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The נר שבת brings peace to the home, because people do not stumble around in the dark. A refugee with no home cannot light it, so he has lost that 'peace.' This also ties the verse to the main topic of the פרק, which is lighting the שבת lamp.
steps.whyThisMatters: This fits the well-known idea, stated earlier in this מסכת (23b), that the נר שבת brings שלום בית.

phrases.english: This is kindling a lamp on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ זוֹ הַדְלָקַת נֵר בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about 'peace'
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'peace' is lighting the נר שבת

steps.title: The lost goodness is the bathhouse
steps.stepSummary: Moving to the second half of the verse, רבי ירמיה says 'goodness' is the bathhouse.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'I forgot goodness': רבי ירמיה said: This is the bathhouse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second half of the verse. רבי ירמיה says the 'goodness' the exile forgot is the bathhouse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'נשיתי טובה' work as an unspoken question: what is this goodness? רבי ירמיה's answer ties directly back to the earlier praise of washing in hot water before שבת.

phrases.notes: The גמרא is quietly asking here: what is this 'goodness' that was forgotten?

steps.triggerLanguage: נָשִׁיתִי טוֹבָה אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה זוֹ בֵּית הַמֶּרְחָץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first half of the verse to the second half

steps.title: Goodness is washing hands and feet in hot water
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says 'goodness' is washing hands and feet in hot water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: This is washing hands and feet in hot water.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a second explanation of 'goodness': washing one's hands and feet in hot water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explanation is smaller than רבי ירמיה's. Even the simple comfort of washing hands and feet with warm water is called 'goodness,' and the exile has lost even that.

phrases.english: This is washing hands and feet in hot water.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן זוֹ רְחִיצַת יָדַיִם וְרַגְלַיִם בְּחַמִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, alternative explanation of 'goodness'
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'goodness' is washing hands and feet in hot water

steps.title: Goodness is a nice bed with nice bedding
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק נפחא says 'goodness' is a pleasant bed and the pleasant linens on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק נפחא said: This is a nice bed and the nice bedclothes on it.
steps.whatsHappening: A third explanation: the 'goodness' is a comfortable bed with nice bedding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This view moves away from washing to another basic comfort of a settled home. A wanderer in exile has no fine bed to sleep in.

phrases.english: and pleasant bedclothes that are on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִצְחָק נַפָּחָא אָמַר זוֹ מִטָּה נָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third explanation of 'goodness'
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'goodness' is a nice bed with nice bedding

steps.title: Goodness is a made bed and an adorned wife
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא says 'goodness' is a made bed and a wife adorned for תלמידי חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said: This is a made bed and a wife adorned for תלמידי חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: A fourth explanation: the 'goodness' is a prepared bed and a wife who is adorned, as befits תלמידי חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבא adds the warmth of a stable home and family life to the comfort of the bed. An exile has lost these as well.

keyTerms.meaning: Made up (a bed spread with linens)

steps.whatToRemember: There is one view on 'peace': lighting the נר שבת. There are four views on 'goodness': the bathhouse, washing hands and feet in hot water, a nice bed, and a made bed with an adorned wife.

phrases.english: and a wife adorned for Torah scholars.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר זוֹ מִטָּה מוּצַּעַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The fourth and last explanation of 'goodness'
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'goodness' is a made bed and an adorned wife

steps.title: Who is wealthy? One who enjoys his wealth
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks who is wealthy. רבי מאיר answers: anyone who has peace of mind from his wealth. A memory sign for the four תנאים follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: Who is wealthy? Anyone who has satisfaction from his wealth. These are the words of רבי מאיר. The memory sign is מטק״ס.
steps.whatsHappening: Because the גמרא was just talking about the good things in life, it brings a ברייתא about who counts as truly rich. רבי מאיר gives the first answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר defines wealth by how a person feels, not by how much he owns. The sign מטק״ס stands for מאיר, טרפון, עקיבא and יוסי, the four תנאים whose views come next.

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ נַחַת רוּחַ בְּעׇשְׁרוֹ,
phrases.english: Anyone who has satisfaction from his wealth,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brought in because it relates to the theme of 'goodness' and prosperity
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, a wealthy person is one who enjoys and is satisfied with what he has.

steps.title: רבי טרפון: a hundred vineyards, fields, and servants
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון says a wealthy person owns a hundred vineyards, a hundred fields, and a hundred servants who work them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי טרפון says: Anyone who has a hundred vineyards, a hundred fields, and a hundred servants working in them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי טרפון gives a second definition of wealth, which is very large holdings of property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike רבי מאיר, רבי טרפון measures wealth by what a person actually owns. In his view, a rich person has huge estates and workers to run them.

phrases.english: Anyone who has one hundred vineyards
and one hundred slaves who work in them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second opinion in the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wealthy person owns very large amounts of property.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: a wife with fine deeds
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says a wealthy person is anyone who has a wife whose actions are pleasant.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: Anyone who has a wife who is pleasant in her deeds.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא gives a third definition: true wealth is a wife of good character.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא measures wealth by the quality of a person's home life, not by money or land.

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ אִשָּׁה נָאָה בְּמַעֲשִׂים.
phrases.english: Anyone who has a wife who is pleasant in her deeds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third opinion in the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wealthy person has a wife of good character.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: a bathroom near his table
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says a wealthy person has a bathroom close to his table.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: Anyone who has a bathroom near his table.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי gives the fourth and last definition: wealth is having a bathroom close to where one eats.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In those days bathrooms were usually far from the house. Having one at home, close by, was a sign of comfort and of good health.
steps.whatToRemember: There are four views on who is wealthy: רבי מאיר says satisfaction, רבי טרפון says large property, רבי עקיבא says a good wife, and רבי יוסי says a nearby bathroom.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The fourth and last opinion in the ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wealthy person has a bathroom close to his table.

steps.title: One may not light with balsam sap
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: one may not light the שבת lamp with צרי (balsam sap).
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: One may not light with balsam sap.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the main topic of the פרק, which fuels may be used for the שבת lamp. It quotes a ruling that צרי is not allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new rule about lighting fuel. The reason is not given yet, and the next step asks for it.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
One may not light with balsam sap.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר אֵין מַדְלִיקִין בִּצְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion of wealth and returns to the laws of שבת lamp fuels
steps.mimraCoreRuling: צרי may not be used as fuel for the שבת lamp.

steps.title: Why is balsam sap forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why צרי may not be used. This sets up רבה's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: צרי burns, so it is not obviously a bad fuel. The גמרא wants to know what the problem is.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the ruling just quoted
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason that צרי is forbidden as lamp fuel

steps.title: Its nice smell might tempt someone to take some
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that because צרי smells pleasant, the חכמים worried that a person would take some from the burning lamp.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: Since its smell spreads, it is a decree, lest he take some from it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה explains that the rule is a precaution. The sweet smell might lead someone to take some of the sap while the lamp is burning on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking fuel from a burning lamp makes it go out sooner, which counts as a form of extinguishing (מכבה). The problem is not the fuel itself but a safeguard that the חכמים added.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made as a safeguard
He will take some for his own use

steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not that צרי burns badly. It burns fine. The concern is that a person will take some from the lit lamp, which shortens how long it burns.

phrases.english: it is a decree lest he take some from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the reason
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is a גזרה, because the pleasant smell might lead a person to take sap from the lit lamp.

steps.title: אביי begins to respond to רבה
steps.stepSummary: אביי starts speaking to רבה. His words continue on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. אביי is about to respond to רבה's reason, and his actual words appear in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This passage is cut off here. When the phrase 'אמר ליה' follows a teacher's explanation, it usually introduces a challenge, so expect אביי to question רבה's reasoning.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces אביי's response to רבה, which continues on the next amud
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's explanation that the concern is taking sap because of its smell
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Not yet stated on this amud; it will appear in the next section.
